extracted.intended_audience: applicants and recipients of NIH construction, modernization, or major alteration & renovation (A&R) grants — grant administrators, institutional officials, project managers, and contracting officers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for planning, designing, procuring, constructing, insuring, using, monitoring, and closing out facilities funded in whole or in part by NIH construction, modernization, or major A&R grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH design review and release of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds for construction, modernization, or major A&R will not be released until the final architectural drawings, specifications, construction schedule, and updated cost estimates are reviewed and approved by the NIH IC unless otherwise indicated in the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release of funds is accomplished by a revised Notice of Award (NoA). The purpose of the NIH design review is to ensure applicable design standards (including 42 CFR Part 52b.12 minimum requirements) are incorporated into working drawings/specifications so program requirements are met and the facility will suitably accommodate planned activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement for bids and procurement review
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisement for bids may be initiated only after approval of the final construction documents by the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement methods to be employed, including plans involving a construction management contract with a GMP clause, must be reviewed and approved by the NIH awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum design requirements (42 CFR Part 52b.12 and NIH Design Requirements Manual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum design requirements for NIH grant-supported construction or modernization are set forth in 42 CFR Part 52b.12 and incorporated in the NIH Design Requirements Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working drawings and specifications submitted for NIH approval must conform to the minimum standards in the NIH Design Requirements Manual. The Manual includes required codes/standards, policies, design standards, and technical criteria for planning, designing, and constructing or altering/renovating buildings owned or leased for NIH use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable codes and standards (state/local and NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are subject to the standards in effect at the time of design or construction and must ensure each project meets applicable State and local codes and ordinances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If State/local codes are proposed in lieu of NIH design requirements, NIH awarding IC must determine that they are equivalent to or exceed NIH requirements. Where State/local codes exceed NIH or regulatory requirements, the more stringent requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended usage requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In planning and designing projects, recipients must consider that the facility is generally subject to an extended usage requirement (e.g., 10 or 20 years) after the date of occupancy and should be constructed accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will monitor compliance with design requirements during design and construction. Recipients with applicability questions should consult the NIH PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of labor standards and equal opportunity in bid documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor standards and equal employment opportunity requirements for federally assisted construction must be specified in information provided to potential bidders/offerors and included in resulting contract documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix II, for contract provisions; NIH construction grants are not subject to Davis-Bacon unless the authorizing statute requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts and subcontracts for construction (including modernization or major A&R) are subject to 41 CFR Part 60-1, implemented by OFCCP and DoL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information available at the Department of Labor OFCCP website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors/subcontractors with construction contracts or subcontracts exceeding $100,000 are subject to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act (40 U.S.C. 3701 et seq.) regarding overtime pay and maintenance of healthful and safe working conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wages must be computed on a 40-hour workweek and overtime paid at not less than 1.5x basic rate. Violations can create liability to employees and potential withholding of funds or liquidated damages; intentional violations carry penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe working conditions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No contractor/subcontractor under an NIH grant shall require any laborer or mechanic to work in surroundings or under conditions that are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to health or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation may be cause for debarment from future Federal contracts or financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of unclaimed wages
rubrics_metrics.description: If employees entitled to wages cannot be located or refuse payment, the recipient may be required to repay the Federal government unless unclaimed wages are placed in escrow and handled per procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient should notify the GMO that an escrow account has been established and maintain it for 2 years (or longer if required by state/local law). After expiration, unclaimed amounts are refunded to NIH proportional to NIH participation. Recipient should document contractors' reasonable efforts to locate employees before taking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of real property management standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction, modernization, and major A&R under research grants are subject to 42 CFR Part 52b; major A&R under center grants or minor A&R under other grants is subject to 2 CFR Part 200.310–200.316 as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory provisions may specify alternate requirements; where statute differs, statutory terms in the award apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on conveyance and encumbrance of grant-funded real property
rubrics_metrics.description: Real property constructed, modernized, or altered with NIH funds may not be conveyed, transferred, assigned, mortgaged, leased, or encumbered except as expressly authorized in writing by NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient defaults on a mortgage they must notify the GMO immediately. Mortgage agreements must allow NIH or its designee to assume the role of mortgagor in default; if NIH does not assume, mortgagee must pay NIH an amount equal to the recipient's share times the Federal share in the property. Any NIH assignment of property/mortgage responsibilities to a party other than NIH requires prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Federal Interest (NFI) recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients shall record a Notice of Federal Interest (NFI) in the appropriate official records where required by 2 CFR Part 200.316 and NIHGPS when use and disposition conditions apply to the property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordation time is when construction begins. Fees may be charged to the grant. A copy of the recorded NFI must be provided to the GMO within 10 days of recordation; contact the GMO for a sample NFI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Builder's risk and post-completion insurance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Builder’s risk insurance is required at the time construction begins; upon completion non-governmental recipients must provide the same type of insurance coverage they maintain for other property, consistent with minimum coverage described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If title vests in recipient, minimum coverage includes: (1) title insurance insuring the fee interest for not less than full appraised value; (2) physical destruction insurance insuring the full appraised value. Policies should cover the total facility when Federal participation covers only a portion. Insurance must be maintained for the duration of the Federal interest. Governmental recipients may follow their own insurance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-insurance waiver criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH awarding IC may waive title or physical destruction insurance if the recipient demonstrates it is effectively self-insured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectively self-insured means the recipient has sufficient funds (e.g., endowment or special funds) to repair/replace the facility or satisfy liens; recipient must provide assurance stating source of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of facility during Federal interest period
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH construction grants require that the facility be used for biomedical or behavioral research for the period prescribed in the NoA; recipient must use the facility for the originally authorized purpose unless prior approval is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficial occupancy defined as when facility conforming to NIH-approved design is available for occupancy and fully operational. NIH will periodically survey recipients (e.g., at least every two years), may request self-certification, and may conduct site visits. After required usage period NIH generally stops direct monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and alternate use approval
rubrics_metrics.description: When use and disposition conditions apply, the recipient may not convey/transfer/encumber property without prior written approval. If facility is no longer needed before expiration of Federal interest, recipient must request written disposition instructions prior to irreversible commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deciding on alternate use NIH will consider extent facility will be used for other health-related purposes consistent with program statute, IC mission, or training/instruction in health fields. Usage obligation may be transferred to another facility with NIH approval; remaining obligations transfer with it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Federal share for amortized acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For property acquired on an amortized acquisition basis, the Federal share of real property acquired with long-term debt financing will be computed for each year Federal funds are used to meet part of the down payment and/or mortgage principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply per-year computation for Federal share where long-term debt financing used during grant-supported years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real estate appraisal standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If a real estate transaction funded in whole/part by NIH requires an appraisal, the appraisal must be performed by appraisers certified or licensed by the State in accordance with Title XI of FIRREA (Public Law 101-73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to appraisals determining Federal share, required insurance levels, and similar valuation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs and activities for construction/modernization/Major A&R
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy lists generally allowable costs and activities under NIH construction/modernization grants and major A&R projects, unless otherwise noted in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable items include acquisition and installation of fixed equipment; appraisals; architectural & engineering services; bid advertising; bid guarantees and performance/payment bonds (per 2 CFR 200.326 and 200.427); contingency fund (≤15% before bids, must be reduced to 10% after contract award; NIH may retain up to 3% control); filing fees for NFI; force account labor if documented as less expensive and approved; general conditions (e.g., site trailers, port-a-johns, hard hats); inspection/commissioning fees; insurance (builder’s risk, title, physical destruction, liability); legal fees related to title; pre-award costs for architect/consultant/environmental analysis if project later funded; profit/fee for contractors consistent with commercial practice; project management; relocation expenses under Uniform Relocation Assistance; sidewalks necessary for facility use; site survey/soil investigation; site clearance (if in bid); threat-risk assessment; NEPA and historic preservation analysis and studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable costs and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy lists costs and activities generally unallowable under NIH construction/modernization grants and major A&R projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable items include bonus payments to contractors (other than earned incentives under formal incentive arrangements), construction of shell space designed for future completion, consultant fees not related to actual construction, damage judgment suits, equipment purchased via conditional sales contracts, fundraising expenses, indirect costs, interior/exterior decorating fees (artwork, sculpture), land acquisition, landscaping/irrigation costs, legal services not related to title certification, movable equipment, and off-site improvements (e.g., parking lots). Lists are not all-inclusive; consult NoA and program guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval requirements for project/budget changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must obtain written prior approval from the GMO for specified recipient-initiated project or budget changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires prior approval for changes described in Administrative Requirements—Changes in Project and Budget (IIA), any revision that would change project scope/site/location or materially alter costs/space utilization/financial outlay (including transfers between construction and non-construction), deviations from design requirements, alternate contracting methods, increases in Federal funds needed to complete project, extension of project period (with/without funds), change in use of facility, or transfer of remaining usage obligation to another facility. Requests must include sufficient information for NIH review. Minor contract modifications may be made without prior approval but all change orders must be retained as grant records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements for minor A&R under non-construction grants
rubrics_metrics.description: For approval of minor A&R projects under non-construction grants, two copies of specified documents must be submitted with each request (whether in application or as post-award rebudgeting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: single-line drawing of existing space and proposed alterations; narrative description of proposed functional utilization and equipment requirements prepared by program/admin managers with input from A/E advisors when appropriate. Narrative must include headings as appropriate: general information; functions to be performed; space schedule; list of fixed equipment; cost estimate; special design problems; description of existing/proposed utility systems; plans for accessibility for physically handicapped; provisions for Life Safety Code requirements; length of lease if rented; other information required by program legislation/regulations. If proposed alteration occurs in an incomplete structure, also provide detailed justification for doing work before completion, cost comparison before vs after, and description of specific benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout submission requirements after construction completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of construction/modernization/A&R the recipient should contact the awarding IC GMO and generally must submit specified closeout documents within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closeout documents typically include: final tabulation of net assignable space supported under the award for each program activity; actual cost of construction per gross and net square foot/meter; actual total allowable project costs after construction per gross and net square foot/meter; actual date of beneficial occupancy; simplified floor plan or space assignment drawing in electronic format clearly marking grant-supported space; final record as-built construction documents; electronic submission of the FFR reflecting Federal and non-Federal share when matching required; written assurance signed by the Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) that required insurance coverage is maintained or indication of self-insurance and source of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy and environmental compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants for construction, modernization, or major A&R are subject to various public policy requirements (statute, regulation, EO, or policy) regardless of recipient type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights include: Architectural Barriers Act accessibility and Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards; Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act compliance (for contracts >$100,000); Coastal Zone Management Act consistency with State program; Copeland Act when required; Davis-Bacon when required by statute; Earthquake Hazards Reduction Act and EO on seismic safety (apply in applicable locations); Endangered Species Act; Flood Disaster Protection Act (flood insurance purchase requirements); Lead-Based Paint Poisoning Prevention Act (prohibits lead-based paint in residence construction/rehab); NEPA requirements — NIH will review Environmental and Other Impacts information in the application and determine whether EIS, EA, or No Further Action applies. If EA/EIS required, applicant must conduct review and provide documentation; applicants must provide listing/copies of relevant licenses/permits and identify State/local/regional planning authorities contacted.
